hints: Build a combination by choosing values one at a time and subtracting from what is left. When is a combination finished, and when is a branch hopeless?
Finished when the remainder hits zero; hopeless when it goes below. Both are one comparison at the top of the recursion.
To stop [2,3] and [3,2] both appearing, never look back: a level may reuse the value it just chose, or move forward, but never return to an earlier one.
Sort the values first, and a value larger than the remainder means every later one is too - so the loop can stop rather than skip.
